profile.reading:
Per NTT's own Global Data Centers facility page, this building, NTT Ashburn VA4, is located at 21583 Megawatt Dr., Ashburn, VA 20147, the fourth of nine planned buildings on NTT's 224-megawatt, 78-acre Ashburn campus in Loudoun County's "Data Center Alley." The operator publishes 140,000 square feet of data floor space and 32 megawatts of critical IT load for this specific building; no formal certifications or opening year are stated on the page. NTT's own site lists an identical street address, square footage, and MW figure for the neighboring VA5 building, indicating VA4 and VA5 are twin buildings or pods sharing one campus address rather than a data error in this registry.

Virginia's data center boom is reshaping statewide electricity rates directly relevant to every Ashburn-area facility. In November 2026, the Virginia State Corporation Commission approved new Dominion Energy rates that will raise a typical residential bill by about $16 a month to roughly $165, while creating a new GS-5 rate class specifically for data centers effective January 1, 2027. Under the new rules, data center customers with 25 megawatts or more of demand, a threshold this single building already exceeds on its own, must sign 14-year mandatory contracts, pay a minimum 85% of transmission and distribution costs and a minimum 60% of generation costs regardless of actual usage, and post collateral upfront for grid upgrades, per Inside Climate News's reporting on the SCC decision.

NTT's US Global Data Centers footprint spans seven named campuses in total: Ashburn, Virginia at 224 megawatts; Chicago, Illinois at more than 200 megawatts; Dallas, Texas at 160 megawatts; Hillsboro, Oregon at 126 megawatts; Phoenix, Arizona at 240 megawatts; and a combined Sacramento/Santa Clara, California figure of 68 megawatts, totaling roughly 1,118 megawatts or more of disclosed US capacity, per the operator's own locations page. The US business operates under the NTT DATA Global Data Centers Americas name, the successor brand to RagingWire Data Centers, now under Japan's NTT DATA Group and parent Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corporation, a Tokyo Stock Exchange-listed company not subject to SEC 10-K filing requirements.

reading.body:
NTT's Ashburn VA4 data center publishes 32 MW of IT capacity, accounting for roughly 2.4 percent of the 1,326 MW across Virginia facilities that have disclosed their power budgets.

At standard densities, 32 MW can support between 800 racks for AI training workloads (40 kW per rack) or 3,200 racks for traditional colocation (10 kW per rack). The operator has not published either figure, so the true hardware footprint depends on tenant workload composition. This gap between power and rack count is not incidental, it is the distinction between AI-dense infrastructure and general-purpose colocation.

The facility sits inside Ashburn's data center corridor, one of Virginia's densest concentrations of published capacity. The state has 326 mapped facilities in total, but only 19 have published megawatt figures. This means 1,326 MW is a floor for Virginia's installed capacity, not a ceiling. The vast majority of the state's infrastructure remains dark to public measurement.

The operator has not published grid interconnection details, power pricing, or tenant identity. No certifications appear in the published specifications. Whether this facility runs AI workloads, balances other compute, or serves traditional colocation cannot be read from available data.
